question: What is one of the primary health risks associated with poor healthcare waste management in Nigeria?

options.A: Transmission of bloodborne pathogens like HIV and Hepatitis
options.B: Decreased prevalence of chronic lifestyle diseases
options.C: Rapid improvement of community water quality

explanation: Improper medical waste disposal exposes individuals to bloodborne pathogens such as HIV and Hepatitis B and C through accidental injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which Nigerian agencies collaborate to establish and enforce environmental and health standards for waste management?

options.A: Ministry of Agriculture and Central Bank
options.B: Federal Ministry of Environment and NESREA
options.C: Ministry of Aviation and Road Safety Corps

explanation: The Federal Ministry of Environment, along with agencies like NESREA and the Federal Ministry of Health, sets guidelines for healthcare waste. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h1)

question: Approximately what percentage of total waste generated in a healthcare facility is classified as general, non-hazardous waste?
explanation: General waste makes up the vast majority of hospital waste, typically ranging between 75% and 90% of the total volume generated. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is considered a sharp and requires specialized hazardous waste management?

options.B: Used infusion sets, needles, and scalpels
options.C: Leftover food scraps from patient trays
options.D: Plastic water bottles and disposable cups

explanation: Sharps include needles, scalpels, and infusion sets that can cause puncture wounds and transmit infections if not handled correctly. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary objective of waste minimization in healthcare settings?

options.A: To increase the total volume of waste requiring incineration
options.B: To reduce the volume and toxicity of waste produced
options.C: To eliminate the need for any waste containers
options.D: To maximize the purchase of single-use plastics

explanation: Waste minimization focuses on reducing both the total volume and the toxicity of the waste generated by healthcare facilities. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h3)

question: Which inventory practice helps prevent pharmaceutical waste generation?

options.A: Overstocking medications close to their expiration dates
options.B: Purchasing expired drugs at a discounted rate
options.C: Careful inventory management to prevent drug expiration
options.D: Storing all medications in unsealed, open containers

explanation: Proper inventory management ensures drugs do not expire on the shelf, thereby preventing avoidable pharmaceutical waste. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h3)

question: Why is segregation at the point of origin considered the most critical step in waste management?

options.A: It prevents hazardous waste from contaminating general waste streams
options.B: It eliminates the need for any protective clothing
options.C: It allows all hospital waste to be recycled as household rubbish
options.D: It reduces the workload of administrative staff only

explanation: Sorting waste immediately at its source prevents hazardous items from mixing with safe general waste, which would otherwise contaminate the entire batch. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h4)

question: What type of container must be strictly used for disposing of used needles and scalpels?
explanation: Sharps must always be placed into puncture-proof safety boxes to prevent accidental needle-stick injuries to staff and handlers. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h4)

question: At what capacity should waste bags and safety boxes be securely closed and collected?
explanation: Containers should be closed and collected when they reach three-quarters (75%) full to prevent overfilling, spills, and accidental punctures. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h5)

question: What personal protective equipment is essential for personnel handling and collecting healthcare waste?

options.A: Sterile surgical gloves and paper caps
options.B: Heavy-duty utility gloves, aprons, and boots
options.C: Regular street clothes and open sandals
options.D: Lead aprons and radiation badges only

explanation: Heavy-duty utility gloves, protective aprons, and sturdy boots protect waste handlers from punctures, chemical splashes, and infectious materials. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is a key requirement for the design of a temporary healthcare waste storage room?

options.A: Carpeted floors to absorb any accidental liquid spills
options.B: Open access for scavengers and the general public
options.C: Washable, impervious floors and walls with proper drainage
options.D: Direct exposure to sunlight to naturally sterilize the room

explanation: Storage areas must have impervious, washable surfaces and drainage to facilitate regular cleaning, disinfection, and infection control. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h6)

question: Why is refrigeration sometimes necessary for storing certain types of hazardous waste, such as pathological waste, in tropical climates?

options.A: To prevent rapid putrefaction, decay, and unpleasant odors
options.B: To freeze the waste into solid blocks for easier burning
options.C: To transform infectious waste into general domestic waste
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of municipal electricity

explanation: In warm climates, organic and pathological waste decomposes quickly, making refrigeration essential to prevent putrefaction and severe odors. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h6)

question: How does an autoclave primarily treat infectious healthcare waste and sharps?

options.A: By burning waste at temperatures exceeding 1500°C
options.B: By exposing the waste to high-pressure, high-temperature steam
options.C: By dissolving the waste entirely in concentrated sulfuric acid
options.D: By burying the waste deep underground without prior treatment

explanation: Autoclaves use high-pressure, high-temperature steam to sterilize infectious materials and destroy pathogens effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is a major environmental concern associated with poorly managed or outdated single-chamber incinerators?

options.A: Release of toxic air pollutants like dioxins and furans
options.B: Excessive production of clean drinking water
options.C: Complete elimination of carbon dioxide emissions
options.D: Transformation of hazardous waste into edible compost

explanation: Improper incineration without modern emission controls releases harmful pollutants such as dioxins and furans into the atmosphere. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is considered the single most effective intervention for preventing the spread of infections in healthcare settings?

options.A: Wearing double surgical masks during all shifts
options.B: Proper hand hygiene using soap and water or hand rubs
options.C: Applying strong chemical disinfectants to patient skin
options.D: Limiting patient visits to once per week

explanation: Hand hygiene is universally recognized as the most effective measure to prevent the transmission of healthcare-associated infections. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h8)

question: What immediate action should a nurse take following an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Ignore the injury since minor scratches pose no risk
options.B: Wash the affected area immediately, report the incident, and seek PEP
options.C: Cover the wound with adhesive tape and finish the shift without telling anyone
options.D: Soak the entire hand in industrial bleach for one hour

explanation: Washing the site immediately, reporting the incident, and evaluating for post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) are critical steps to mitigate infection risks. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h8)
